The cost spike on 2025-10-20 for account xz8lX1K comes from one instance family, **QI78eHTqNo**. It runs only in application 6IN on GCP cloud service zjTD5.

**What the data shows:**
- **Account level:** GCP cost went from about 5,270 a day to 6,810 on Oct 20 and stayed high on Oct 21 (6,768). It fell back to about 5,575 on Oct 22. AWS and Azure stayed flat.
- **Service level:** Within GCP, the increase is almost all in cloud service zjTD5, which went from about 1,230 to 2,746 a day.
- **Instance family level:** Within zjTD5, the increase is all in instance family QI78eHTqNo. Its daily cost was:

| Date | Cost |
|---|---|
| Oct 16 | 318 |
| Oct 17 | 382 |
| Oct 18 | 64 |
| Oct 19 | 64 |
| **Oct 20** | **1,592** |
| **Oct 21** | **1,497** |
| Oct 22 | 350 |

  That is about 946 above its previous-week average, the largest increase of any instance family. No other instance family in application 6IN moved meaningfully.

**Why I left out two other changes on the same day:** in AWS, application sDS (cloud service 3wTal) rose by about 454 and application kPE (cloud service pHsZR) fell by about 354. These mostly cancel out, and total AWS cost didn't change. That pattern looks like a workload moving between the two rather than an anomaly, so I didn't count either as a root cause.

I reported the root cause at the instance family level. Application 6IN would be an equally valid way to name the same spike.
